title: Retry 2ms5: fix main CI shard 1 failure and record red main CI
summary: Retry of job 20261107-120506-2ms5, which failed in planning before any code was written (no candidate kept). Find the test failing in main CI 'test (shard 1)' after the three named landings, name it and its root cause from the logs, fix the cause, and make Athena record a red main CI result after a landing so the next baseline notes it. The plan must use only verifier-runnable demonstrations and list every touched file as a deliverable.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the named test passing on repeat and the red-CI note appearing in the baseline.
The fix targets the cause of the failure, not a retry or skip.
Criteria run tests and the status command rather than check that files exist.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261107-120506-2ms5 addressed: it ended failed in planning (round 1 of 5) with no candidate, so no changed file is kept and nothing is dropped. Its findings are fixed as follows: the one major finding (a disallowed demonstration command with output redirection) is fixed by naming each demonstration as its own simple command with no redirection, and the five minor findings (files outside the deliverables: crates/athena-data/src/records/plan.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs, crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs) are fixed by listing those paths as deliverables here.

Goal and audience: the Athena maintainer and the next job's planner and verifier. They need a named root cause for the red main CI and a baseline that shows red main CI after a landing instead of staying silent.

Environment: the GitHub Actions site for this repository's main-branch 'test (shard 1)' push runs, read through `gh run view --log-failed`, read-only; plus the repository git history read with `git log`, read-only. They reach CI logs, run results and commit times of landings. Nothing is pushed or written outside the working copy. If the logs cannot be read, the fix is argued from the code and the gap is stated in CHANGELOG.md.

Code survey: entry points are the CLI drain and status in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, the snapshot and status figures in crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs and crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, and baseline building in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs and crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs. Record parsing lives in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs and crates/athena-data/src/records/plan.rs. A new record kind or field must be accepted by the records validation allow-list, and its round-trip test, `check_record_file` or `AnyRecord`, must cover it. The landing time and the other throughput figures are measured from landing records in the snapshot, not through a stand-in. Run order: drain lands, records are written, then the baseline reads them.

Existing code: the change extends crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs, crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs and crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, and reuses the existing baseline note path rather than adding a new one.
The failing test and its cause are unknown until the logs are read. The fix must address shared state, ordering or timing in the test or the code it covers, not retry, ignore or skip.
Standing defaults applied: tested (fmt, clippy and test pass), root-cause, behavior-evidence and verified.
Consumers: none found, because no config file is changed.

acceptance_criteria.text: CHANGELOG.md has an entry naming the failing test and its panic message as read from the 'test (shard 1)' logs of the push runs after 20261107-031902-ttnw, 20261107-031925-mrpk and the 2026-11-06 mirror-check landing. It says whether the failure is intermittent, gives the root cause, and states only what the diff does.
The diff changes the cause of the failure in the test or the code it covers, not a retry, ignore or skip attribute. A regression test in the diff fails on the old code and passes on the new.

Run `cargo test --locked` on the changed tree: the named test passes. Run `cargo test <test name>` a second time to show a repeat pass. Athena's recorded test check on the same final tree also counts.

Red main CI recording: a test in the diff feeds sample records holding a failed main CI result after a landing and checks that the baseline notes it. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` and `cargo test -p athena-data`. The test fails when the new recording code is reverted.

Real records check: run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot evidence` as one simple command with no redirection, on the real records. The landing time it prints must be within the expected range taken from the commit times of landings in history.json and `git log`, which this change does not compute. Landings take a few minutes each, so 0.1 minutes or hundreds of minutes is a failure. Attempts per landed change, wasted spend and first-attempt share must equal their output before the change.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` as separate commands; all pass, or the recorded checks on the same final tree show them passed.

Scope: the diff changes only the deliverables and CHANGELOG.md, with no change to athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows or prompt files, and no edit to existing entries under records/ or docs/decisions.md.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or annotating existing records under records/ or docs/decisions.md.
Editing athena.toml, defaults.toml, .gitattributes, workflows or prompt files.
Reverting or redoing jobs 20261107-031902-ttnw and 20261107-031925-mrpk; their landed work is kept.
Changing the throughput review measures, the improvement-turn ordering or the 25% slowdown rule.
Marking the test ignored or adding CI retries to hide the failure.
Changing the planning stage's demonstration-command check or the planner brief (the separate prevention proposed by introspection 20261117-030207-h2w9).
departures: The previous attempt failed in planning and the task needs CI log reading plus a record-baseline change, so cost, time and pass odds are worse than the reference.
hard_reason: It changes what Athena records after a landing and what the next job's baseline reads, which is the run pipeline and records, and it touches a measure computed from records.
